decision.outcome: 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke), time to first event, ITT, on-study
decision.span: ITT analyses (on-study and on-treatment) of MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, and non-fatal stroke, are consistent with those of MACE+ (Table 8). The reason for the similarity is that only 0.3% of subjects in the ITT population experienced hospitalization for unstable angina. For ITT analysis 792 MACE events were observed, 392 and 400 in placebo and lixisenatide group, respectively. The 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio is (0.887, 1.172) with a point estimate of 1.02.
decision.table_span: Table 8: Analysis of the MACE Endpoint | Placebo (N=3,034) | Lixisenatide (N=3,034) | Hazard ratio (95% CI) | MACE endpoint (on-study) 1.02 (0.89, 1.18) | No. of patients with event (%) 392 (12.9%) 400 (13.2%) | Total Person Year 6340.2 6368.7 | Incidence Rate 6.18 6.28
decision.note: The 4-point primary (1.02 [0.89, 1.17]) and the 3-point secondary (1.02 [0.887, 1.172]) are numerically near-identical because only 0.3% had unstable-angina hospitalisation; older reviews that relabelled the 4-point as 3-point reached the right number by luck. This value is the trial's own 3-point analysis, verified by the FDA statistical reviewer.

source_conflict.what_conflicts: the SAME 3-component MACE result (792 events, 392 placebo / 400 lixisenatide, ITT on-study) is printed with three interval renderings: unrounded (0.887, 1.172) in the section text; (0.89, 1.18) in Table 8; (0.89, 1.17) in the executive summary. 1.172 rounds to 1.17, so Table 8's 1.18 is the discrepant rendering. The 4-component primary (MACE+, 805 events, 399/406) is ALSO printed as 1.02 (0.89, 1.17): the interval does NOT identify the endpoint. An independent read (Gemini, 18 Sep; proposals only, verified here against held bytes) also located the 4-point primary's UNROUNDED interval 1.017 (0.886, 1.168) (page 8): the unrounded 3-point (0.887, 1.172) and 4-point (0.886, 1.168) differ; only their rounded forms coincide.
